source.title: Tracing Moral Foundations in Large Language Models
source.authors: Chen-Xiao Yu; Bo-Wen Yi; Farzan Karimi-Malekabadi; Suhaib Abdurahman; Jin Ye; Shrikanth S. Narayanan; Yue Zhao; Morteza Dehghani

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether SAE-recoverable sparse features are present and functionally relevant in LLMs, a new setting for the claim's indirect-evidence version. It does not test toy-model superposition or feature competition.
record.gate_note: Included results on SAE-feature alignment, semantic characterization, and micro-steering. Excluded dense moral-vector geometry and macro-steering because they do not measure SAE-recoverable sparse features. Values used to select layers or features are not treated as outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study treats pretrained SAEs as a tool for decomposing moral concept vectors. It does not test whether models store features in superposition, whether features are spread across neurons, or whether SAEs recover sparse features generally: no reconstruction, sparsity, neuron-polysemanticity or dictionary-quality results. Its SAE results are cosine alignment of decoder directions with the authors' own concept vectors, qualitative labels for hand-filtered top-10 features, and micro- versus macro-steering comparisons. These measure the authors' method and the moral constructs, not any version of the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that moral foundations are separable linear directions that emerge in pretraining and are selectively rewired by post-training. They say these directions decompose into interpretable SAE features, described as partially disentangled. They also say steering along vectors or features causally shifts questionnaire responses. The authors make no claim about superposition itself.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses concept-vector projection, pretrained SAEs, semantic feature characterization, and activation steering in LLMs. It does not reproduce the original toy-network feature competition or sparsity sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: SAE-feature alignment varies by model family and layer: Llama models peak in middle layers, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct has a U-shaped trajectory, and Qwen3-30B-A3B peaks at Layer 39.

fits_no_version.finding: Top-10 SAE decoder directions selected per foundation align with moral concept vectors above a random baseline. The layer profile depends on model family (Llama mid-layer peak; Qwen early/late peaks).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE decoder directions in LLMs align with supervised concept (difference-in-means) directions above chance, with family-dependent layer profiles.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering along the selected top-10 SAE feature directions shifts MFQ-2 scores, often more steeply than dense concept vectors (17/20 cells above y=x, OLS slope 2.57). On Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct this costs MMLU accuracy (about −3.4pp at |ρ|=0.2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Steering along SAE features can move concept-related behavior at least as strongly as steering along dense concept vectors.

fits_no_version.finding: Selected SAE features receive coherent moral-content labels (mostly Care and Authority); no high-confidence Loyalty features were found.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features aligned with a concept vector are interpretable as sub-facets of that concept.

record.problems: SAE-based analyses cover only four models with released SAEs and sampled layers rather than all layers; the authors say this is not an exhaustive search for globally optimal features. Feature semantics are qualitative and based on 50,000 FineWeb documents; no high-confidence Loyalty assignments were obtained. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the feature-alignment and semantic-feature outcomes.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant SAE results omitted.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweep or feature geometry.
No test of capacity competition or importance-based allocation of dimensions.
No analysis of the causes of polysemantic neurons; polysemanticity is only cited.
No measure of features being spread across neurons, and no test of SAE reconstruction or sparsity, or of how many interpretable features an SAE recovers. Pretrained SAEs are used as given.
No test of completeness, stability or canonicity of SAE features.

record.verdict_notes: The record over-reads the SAE results as tests of V4. The paper only cites Toy Models of Superposition for neuron polysemanticity and uses off-the-shelf SAEs (Llama Scope, Qwen-Scope, community SAEs) as instruments. Every SAE outcome is conditioned on top-10 selection by cosine to the authors' own vectors, plus filtering of the GPT labels.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test toy networks, overcomplete sparse feature storage, overlap, near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry.
Does not test whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition or whether feature importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Does not investigate alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
Tests whether sparse SAE features can be identified in selected LLMs; does not test whether features are spread across neurons, and covers only models and layers with available SAEs.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable across runs or dictionaries, or canonical units of the model.
Does not test the dimensionality of superposed features; using one-dimensional concept and decoder directions for analysis is not a test of whether model features are intrinsically one-dimensional.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B-Base
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine alignment between foundation vectors and top-10 SAE decoder features across sampled layers.
rows.measure: Average cosine similarity of top-10 SAE features to moral-foundation concept vectors
rows.baseline: Random baseline; numeric value not stated
rows.value: Alignment substantially exceeds the random baseline across all layers; peaks at Layer 19 across all five foundations.
rows.note: The text describes the trend and peak; plotted cosine values are not transcribed.
rows.check: Measures cosine between selected SAE decoder directions and the study's moral concept vectors versus a random baseline. That is concept-to-feature alignment under top-10 selection, not evidence that the model contains SAE-recoverable sparse features. The values are only in Figure 8a, which is not transcribed.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine alignment between foundation vectors and top-10 SAE decoder features across sampled layers.
rows.measure: Average cosine similarity of top-10 SAE features to moral-foundation concept vectors
rows.baseline: Random baseline; numeric value not stated
rows.value: Alignment substantially exceeds the random baseline across all layers; peaks at Layer 15 across all five foundations. Care and Sanctity align more highly than Loyalty and Authority.
rows.note: The text describes the trend and peak; plotted cosine values are not transcribed.
rows.check: Same as r1 (Figure 8b). This is a selection-based alignment measure tied to the study's own vectors.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine alignment between foundation vectors and top-10 SAE decoder features across sampled layers.
rows.measure: Average cosine similarity of top-10 SAE features to moral-foundation concept vectors
rows.baseline: Random baseline; numeric value not stated
rows.value: Alignment starts high at Layer 3, dips across Layers 7–15, and rises again, peaking at Layer 23; Fairness has the highest separation at the peak.
rows.note: The text describes the trajectory and peak; plotted cosine values are not transcribed.
rows.check: Same as r1 (Figure 8c). The baseline condition is missing from the conditions, though the text does compare to a random baseline.

rows.subject: Qwen3-30B-A3B
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine alignment between foundation vectors and top-10 SAE decoder features across sampled layers.

conditions.value: low across Layers 7–35, then increases at Layer 39

rows.measure: Average cosine similarity of top-10 SAE features to moral-foundation concept vectors
rows.baseline: Random baseline; numeric value not stated
rows.value: Alignment remains low across Layers 7–35 and increases sharply at Layer 39, especially for Sanctity and Fairness.
rows.note: Feature alignment is concentrated at the final sampled layer rather than evident throughout the sampled depth.
rows.check: Same as r1 (Figure 8d). The 'partial' state refers to the layer profile of moral alignment, not to any superposition version.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Characterized selected SAE features using top-activating FineWeb contexts and GPT-5.1 summaries with human validation.
rows.measure: Semantic coherence of selected SAE features
rows.value: Reported feature examples include distinct Care patterns for physical suffering and emotional distress, and Authority patterns for institutions, roles, and frameworks.
rows.note: Feature descriptions were generated by GPT-5.1 and human-validated; this is qualitative evidence, not an exhaustive feature inventory.
rows.check: Qualitative GPT-5.1 labels for features pre-selected by cosine and filtered by the paper. These are exemplars, not an outcome rate; the existence of interpretable SAE features is assumed, not tested.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Characterized selected SAE features using top-activating FineWeb contexts and GPT-5.1 summaries with human validation.
rows.measure: Semantic coherence of selected SAE features
rows.value: Reported feature examples include Care-related bullying, compassion, and health/safety patterns; Authority-related government and legal patterns; and a Fairness-related corporate-practice pattern.
rows.note: Feature descriptions were generated by GPT-5.1 and human-validated; this is qualitative evidence, not an exhaustive feature inventory.

rows.measure: Semantic coherence of selected SAE features

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B-Base, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, and Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Steered activations along decoder directions of selected top-10 SAE features.

conditions.value: micro-feature steering versus matched macro-vector steering

rows.value: 17/20 cells lie above the y = x diagonal; OLS slope 2.57.
rows.note: The paper reports these results only as an aggregate across four SAE-equipped models and 20 model-foundation cells.
rows.check: Compares the study's own micro-steering with its macro-steering (17/20 cells above y=x). This is a method comparison, not a measure of superposition or of SAE feature recovery.

rows.subject: Four SAE-equipped models (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Counted high-confidence semantic assignments to moral foundations in the SAE feature-mining analysis.
rows.baseline: Other foundations were identified; no numeric comparison stated
rows.value: No high-confidence Loyalty/Betrayal assignments were obtained in the semantic-mining pass.
rows.note: Authors attribute this to the limited validation sample and compute budget, not to absence of Loyalty-related signal.
rows.check: Reports a gap in the semantic-mining pass, which the authors attribute to sample and compute limits. It is not a model result bearing on any version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Four SAE-equipped LLMs; selected SAE layers and features
reader_labels.reason: Selected sparse features align with moral vectors, yield coherent semantic descriptions, and feature-direction steering changes MFQ-2 scores (r1–r9).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Across sampled layers, foundations, and available SAE models
reader_labels.reason: Feature alignment varies substantially by model and depth; no high-confidence Loyalty assignments were found, and the SAE analysis is restricted to available models and layers (r3, r4, r10).
